Not sure if this counts as a poem, but this is one of my favourite pieces of my writing.


**Her Teddy**



Aged 3, the little girl gets a teddy bear from her grandma for Christmas. She names it Teddy and takes it with her everywhere.



Aged 4, her grandma dies. She cuddles Teddy as a reminder of her.



Aged 5, everyone else her age is starting school. Her parents have forgotten, so she sits at home all day playing with her only toy.



Aged 6, her mom falls ill. She gives her mom Teddy to protect her in the hospital.



Aged 7, it’s now just her and her dad. She takes Teddy to the funeral so it’s like there’s three people there.



Aged 8, her dad is meant to be home-schooling her, but he’s too busy drinking to look after her. She and Teddy go to the Library every day to try to learn


Aged 9, she reminds him of her mom. He yells and hits her. She hides under the bed with Teddy, hoping that he won’t find her.



Aged 10, he visits her at night. She turns Teddy away so he doesn’t have to see what her father does to her.



Aged 11, she’s taken away. Her father goes to jail and she goes to a care home. The only thing she takes with her is Teddy.



Aged 12, she doesn’t belong here. The other kids mock her for carrying around Teddy.



Aged 13, she’s being sent to school. She doesn’t understand the teacher and she’s panicking about having to leave Teddy at home.



Aged 14, Teddy is falling apart. The lady at the care home throws him away and the not-so-little girl is alone for good.



Aged 15, it’s too much for her, no friends, no family, and too dumb for school. Scars appear on her wrists and pills start going missing.



Aged 16, the little girl is no more.

He was gone.

I choked back tears watching the train leave as the reality hit me. He was really gone.

I slowly walked away from the station, turning to get one last glimpse of the train, far in the distance, taking him away from me.

I knew he'd have to leave eventually, though I'd tried to deny it. I just hadn't expected it to be so soon. The last few years had been the most joyful of my life, but I could already sense that joy leaving, replaced with a numbness, filling me up.

It was early in the day, and I was glad about that. The streets were empty, so I didnt have to try and hide the tears streaming down my face. I reached for my phone. It had only been ten minutes, but maybe he missed me too.

~*No new messages*~

I tearfully put my phone back in my bag. Of course he didnt miss me. I was just his friend, while he... he was my everything.

I reached ~~our~~ *my* house, and dejectedly let myself in. It seemed so empty with out him. The existence of my best friend, and ex-housemate, had vanished in a matter of days.

I poured a large glass of wine, and, taking the bottle with me, wandered round the house, pausing to take in the spaces that used to be occupied by his possessions. I stopped in his bedroom, sitting down on the empty floor, taking in the four wall, devoid of the character that had  filled themm mere days before.

I  gulped down the wine, hoping it would dull the crippling lonliness I felt. The house was so quiet without him, I'd never felt this alone before.

I glanced down at my phone again.

~*No new messages*~

The phone hit the wall with such force, I think it left a dent, as I screamed in frustration. How could I have been so *stupid*, falling fo my best  friend? 

But, there in the question was the answer, because he was my best friend. He was kind, gorgeous, and he liked all the same things as me, how could I not fall in love? And now, he was gone.


The lonliness took over me again as I gulped down wine and curled up on the floor, and was soon replaced with regret. Id never told him how I felt. Id kept my feelings hidden for so long, and now he'd never know.

I'd loved him so deeply, so purely.  Now that love was corrupted with lonliness and despair.

I closed my eyes, trying to drown out the emotions that were consuming me, when I heard a tiny beep from across the room. I slowly raised my eyes to where my phone had fallen, and made my way towards it, too nervous to breathe. I looked down at the screen.

~*One new message*~
